I5.quote: A series of bimetallic Pd–Fe catalysts supported on ordered mesoporous carbon (denoted as Pd1–FeX/OMC) were prepared with a variation Fe/Pd molar ratio (X), and they were applied to the catalytic decomposition of phenethyl phenyl ether to aromatics.

notes: Catalysis paper (Pd-Fe on ordered mesoporous carbon for lignin model-compound decomposition). The only hydrogen amount reported is from thermal desorption: Table 3 'Amount of desorbed hydrogen (μmol-H2/g-cat.)', footnote 'Calculated from peak area of H2-TPD profile (<600 °C)' (main, p. 6, journal p. 189, Table 3). The H2-TPD method states '5% H2/Ar mixed gas (50 mL/min) was injected for 60 min at 250 °C ... The desorbed hydrogen was detected using a TCD' (main, p. 3, journal p. 186, Section 2.2); the uptake during the H2/Ar flow step is not measured, so this is TPD alone. H2-TPR (hydrogen consumption during reduction, Fig. 6) and the 250 °C, 10 bar H2 catalytic reaction (Table 2) are reactions of hydrogen without a measured uptake. I1 fails and the paper is neither theoretical nor electrochemical, so the code is no_conditions_stated; I2-I4 not assessed. For information only: BET surface areas of 732-782 m2/g are reported for all catalysts (Table 1, main p. 5). not_primary, retracted (record is_retracted false; no retraction notice in the PDF) and duplicate_data do not apply.
